Q: Using group_by with user defined function A:

Here is another solution. First count the positives in Student.Attended == "Yes".
Then, filter those and compute the percentage of entryby19 == "Yes".
Finally, join the two results above by the grouping variable, Type.

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))

example <- tibble(Student.ID = c("#001","#002","#003","#004","#005"),
                  Student.Attended = c("Yes", "Yes", "No", "Yes", "Yes"), 
                  entryby19 = c("Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "No"),
                  Type = c("Exhibition", "Exhibition", "Mentoring", "Mentoring", "Mentoring"))

progressionby19 <- function(.data, .by) {
  .data %>%
    summarise(
      count = sum(Student.Attended == "Yes"),
      .by = {{ .by }}
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      .data %>%
        filter(Student.Attended == "Yes") %>%
        summarise(
          progression_rate = mean(entryby19 == "Yes") * 100,
          .by = {{ .by }}
        ),
      by = join_by({{ .by }})
    )
}

example %>%
  progressionby19(.by = Type)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   Type       count progression_rate
#>   <chr>      <int>            <dbl>
#> 1 Exhibition     2              100
#> 2 Mentoring      2               50
